rejected.title: The Great Leap Forward
card: The Great Leap Forward began in 1958. Mao Zedong wanted China to industrialise fast and catch up with Britain in steel output within a few years, using its huge population instead of costly machines.
Farming villages were merged into large people's communes. A commune ran farming, small industry, meals and schooling, and families gave up private plots.
Peasants were told to make steel in small backyard furnaces. Many left the fields to do it, and the steel was often poor. Local officials reported inflated grain figures to look successful.

The state took grain based on those false figures, leaving too little food in villages. Bad weather made it worse. A famine followed from about 1959 to 1961, and millions died. Estimates of the toll vary widely, often from 15 to 45 million.
rejected.remember: Mao's fast industrial drive through communes cut farm output and hid the shortfall, and a famine killed millions.

a.q: Why did the Great Leap Forward lead to famine?
opts: Farm work was cut and grain demands used false reports
Landlords took back land and held grain from peasants
Other countries ended all trade and sold China no grain
Communes were abolished and peasants left farming at once
a.why: Peasants left the fields for steel and other work, and officials overstated harvests, so the state took too much grain. Landlords had lost their land in land reform and had no part in it, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about where workers went and what officials reported.

b.q: In 1959 a commune official in Henan reports a record harvest that never happened. What is the most likely result for the villagers?
opts: The state takes more grain than they can spare
The state sends extra grain to help them
Their commune is freed from planning targets
Their harvest is raised by the extra attention
b.why: The state based its grain demands on reported figures. An inflated figure meant the state took grain the village could not spare, leaving too little to eat. Extra help would suit a bad report, not a good one.
b.clue: What did the state use to decide how much grain to take?
